issues.legal_issue: The statutory presumption that a promissory note was made for consideration does not arise when the claimant pleads consideration different from that recited in the note.
material_facts: The suit sought recovery on a promissory note that recited cash consideration.
The claimant pleaded that the note was given in consideration for the transfer of additional land and a building, rather than for cash.
The note’s execution was admitted or proved.
issues.conclusion: Because the pleaded consideration differed from the consideration recited in the note, the initial presumption under Section 118(a) of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, was unavailable to the claimant. The court had to assess the evidence to determine whether the pleaded consideration was established.
issues.legal_principle: Section 118(a) ordinarily requires a court to presume that a proved or admitted negotiable instrument was made for consideration, until the contrary is proved. But where the claimant pleads consideration different from that recited in the instrument, that initial presumption does not arise; the court must evaluate the evidence as a whole. The Court discussed the burden-shifting principles in Kundan Lal Rallaram v. Custodian, Evacuee Property, Bombay, U. Ponnappa Moothan Sons v. Catholic Syrian Bank Ltd., Indian Bank v. K. Nataraja Pillai, G. Ramatulasamma v. K. Gowaraiah, and Y.M. Prasad v. The Sanathnagar Wire Products. Sections 3 and 4 of the Evidence Act inform the meaning of proof and presumptions.

predicates.promissory_note_recovery_suit: A claimant brings a suit to recover an amount on the basis of a promissory note.
predicates.note_execution_established: The maker admits or the evidence establishes that the promissory note was executed.
predicates.pleaded_consideration_differs: The claimant pleads that the note was given for consideration different from that recited in the note.

issues.definition: When a recovery suit is based on an executed promissory note but the claimant pleads a different consideration from the one recited, the statutory presumption of consideration does not arise.

issues.legal_issue: A promissory note is supported by legally enforceable consideration when the evidence establishes that it was given in exchange for delivery of property, even if a related sale agreement later falls through.
material_facts: The promissory note recited cash consideration, but the claimant relied on evidence that additional land and a building were delivered to the maker in exchange for the note.
Oral and documentary evidence, including correspondence and the parties’ conduct, supported the finding that possession of the additional property had been delivered.
The related agreement to sell other land was not completed, but the courts found that the additional property had been delivered in consideration for the note.
issues.conclusion: The additional property was delivered in consideration for the promissory note, and that transfer was legally enforceable consideration. The concurrent findings supporting recovery disclosed no illegality warranting interference, so the decree was upheld and the appeal dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 118(a) of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, concerns whether a negotiable instrument was made for consideration; where its initial presumption is unavailable, the court must determine from the evidence whether consideration actually passed. The consideration need not be the cash recited in the instrument if another valid consideration is established. The Court applied the evidentiary approach discussed in Kundan Lal Rallaram v. Custodian, Evacuee Property, Bombay, and G. Ramatulasamma v. K. Gowaraiah, and held that the evidence of property delivery, correspondence, and the parties’ conduct established consideration in this case.

predicates.promissory_note_recovery_appeal: An appeal challenges a decree granting recovery on the basis of a promissory note.
predicates.property_possession_transferred_for_note: The claimant delivered possession of property to the maker in exchange for the promissory note.
predicates.evidence_supports_property_transfer: Oral or documentary evidence, including the parties’ conduct, supports the finding that possession was delivered in exchange for the note.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns recovery on a promissory note and evidence supports a finding that property was delivered in exchange for it, the note is supported by enforceable consideration and the decree is upheld.
